transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

Lately when I’m home alone, I end up eating way more food at once than I think most people would, and it keeps happening. It's gotten to the point where I'm really starting to worry about it, so I decided it was time to talk to someone.
During these episodes of eating large amounts of food, do you feel like you're unable to stop or control what you're doing?

Yeah, absolutely. Once I start, it feels like something clicks off in my brain, and even though I'm telling myself, "Dude, you don't need more," my hands just keep grabbing food. I really can't seem to stop until everything in front of me is completely gone.
After these episodes of eating large amounts of food, do you usually feel guilty or ashamed about what you've done?

Yeah, I feel extremely guilty and disgusted with myself. I usually just sit there staring at the trash, feeling like a total failure and wondering why I did it again. It honestly puts me in this really heavy, dark mood for the rest of the night.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever try to compensate for the amount of food you've eaten by doing things like vomiting, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?
No, I've never done anything like that. I don't try to throw up, take laxatives, or go work out to burn it off. I usually just end up lying in bed feeling miserable.
How often do these episodes of eating large amounts of food happen, and have you noticed any specific triggers that seem to lead to them?

For the last three or four months, it's been happening at least once a week, and often more than that. It usually gets triggered when I'm home alone late at night feeling bored or isolated while gaming, and I just use food as a comfort or a break.

Do you experience significant distress or anxiety related to your eating habits or weight, and do you think about food or your body image even when you're not engaging in these episodes of excessive eating?

Yes, I feel a ton of distress and shame about my body and my eating habits even when I'm not eating. I've become so self-conscious that I've been turning down plans to hang out with friends or play pickup basketball, and those negative feelings just hang over me all the time now. It really keeps me isolated in my room most days.

You mentioned you don't try to compensate by vomiting, laxatives, or excessive exercise, but have you ever restricted your food intake or followed a very strict diet to try to make up for these episodes of overeating?
No, I haven't really tried restricting my food or going on any strict diets to make up for it. I definitely feel super guilty and bad about it, but I don't do any kind of strict dieting.
Can you estimate how many times a month you have these episodes of eating large amounts of food, and are they always associated with feeling bored, isolated, or using food as a comfort?

I'd estimate it happens about 4 to 8 times a month, sometimes even more depending on the week. And yes, they are definitely tied to feeling bored and isolated, especially since I moved back home, lost my daily routine, and started spending so much time alone in my room gaming.

Do you experience any other symptoms like feeling a lack of control over eating, eating rapidly during these episodes, or eating until you feel uncomfortably full, which might help clarify what's going on with your eating habits?

Yeah, I experience all of those. Once I start, it feels like a switch flips in my head and I eat incredibly fast, barely chewing between gaming rounds and finishing everything in ten minutes. I also keep eating past the point where my stomach actually hurts, to where I have to lie back on my bed because I'm so uncomfortably full.
